title: SEO Mistakes Drinks Websites Make | Craft Beer School
desc: The SEO mistakes we see on drinks websites, from age gates that hide content to thin pages and wrong hours, with a fix for each one.
teaser: Most drinks sites lose visitors to a handful of avoidable mistakes. Here is each one and the fix.
standfirst: Good SEO is mostly avoiding self-inflicted damage. These are the mistakes that come up again and again on brewery, winery and spirits sites, with a plain fix for each.
sections: The age gate that blocks everything

Age checks are right for alcohol brands and required in many places. But some are built so that search engines and visitors see nothing else until the gate is passed. Ask your developer how the gate works and test how a crawler sees the page. Make sure the key content is still readable. Keep the age statement clear and honest.

Do not weaken the gate to please search engines. Check your legal duties locally and balance both.
Hidden facts, thin pages and slow loads

A beautiful poster with your hours and address is text to a person but a picture to a search engine. Put name, address, phone and hours as real text on the page and on your Business Profile. Make them identical everywhere.

A page with one line, or with a description pasted from a distributor, gives a visitor nothing and a search engine no reason to show it. Write your own text for each product: style, strength, taste, serve, where to buy. Fewer, fuller pages are better. See content that brings visitors.

Large photos of bottles and venues can make pages slow. Most visitors are on phones, often on a weak connection. Compress images, use sizes that fit the screen and test the site on mobile data. A page that takes too long to appear loses people before they read anything.

Repeating beer near me ten times in a paragraph reads badly and can hurt. Write for people. Do the same with your Business Profile name: adding keywords breaks the platform's rules and can get the listing suspended. Do not list addresses where you do not operate.

Paid link packages and bought reviews are against the rules of search engines and review platforms. At best they do nothing. At worst they bring penalties. Earn links from real stockists, bars, local press and event pages instead.

A single page that tries to be about the brewery, the beers, the tours and the shop cannot be the best answer to any question. Give each topic its own page and link them together. Use the method in keyword research for a brewery website to match each page to what people search.
A quick audit you can do today

Open your site on your phone and check ten things. Does it load in a few seconds? Can you read the hours and address without zooming? Does each beer or product have its own page? Does the booking or enquiry button work? Does the age statement show? Search your own name on Google and see what appears. Search for your venue on Maps and compare the details. Look at your pages in Search Console for errors.

Write down each problem and fix the easiest first. Small corrections to basic facts are usually the highest-value jobs on the list.

Repeat the audit every quarter and after any redesign, because new templates often bring back old faults such as missing titles or an age gate that blocks crawlers.

Fix them in order of effort. Basic facts and hours take minutes. Image sizes and page titles take an afternoon. A rebuilt age gate or a restructured site is a project, so plan it with your developer and test it before it goes live.
Responsible marketing is part of SEO

Content that targets minors, glamorises heavy drinking or makes health claims can break advertising rules, which differ by country and, in India, by state. It can lead to your pages or profiles being removed. Keep the tone moderate, include a responsible drinking line where required and check with a lawyer or the regulator if you are unsure.

Many sites never check whether SEO is working. Set up Search Console and a simple count of bookings and enquiries on day one. Without a baseline you cannot tell a good change from a bad one, or a seasonal swing from a real result.

Anyone who guarantees a first position is guessing or selling. Search engines change their methods, competitors improve and results shift. Aim for a site that is accurate, quick and useful. Measure over months. For the basics, start with SEO for breweries.
faqs: What is the most common mistake?
Wrong or missing basic details such as opening hours and address, followed by thin pages with no real information.
Will fixing these guarantee a better ranking?
No. Nobody can guarantee a ranking. These fixes remove obstacles and make the site more useful.
Should I hire an SEO agency?
Only if they explain their methods, show you how they will measure and promise no ranking. Check what they do against these mistakes.
